newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM says no North merger talks.
newsitem.headline: MIM says no North merger talks.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Monday there were no merger talks in progress with fellow base metals giant North Ltd.
"MIM is not discussing a merger with North," MIM chief executive Nick Stump said.

A MIM spokesman said a report in Monday's edition of The Australian newspaper that North was unhappy about cost overruns and its partnership role in the Alumbrera copper-gold project in Argentina, was pure speculation.
"Alumbrera is going to be one of the world's great mining projects and will be commissioned in the September quarter," the spokesman said.
MIM has a 50 percent stake in the project while North and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd each have 25 percent.
MIM has a market capitalisation of A$2.85 billion based on its Monday closing price of A$1.74 per share, which was steady on the day. It has 1.64 billion shares on issue.
North, a Melbourne-based miner, has a market capitalisation of A$3.01 billion based on 717.6 million shares on issue and a closing price of A$4.20 on Monday. The stock fell three cents on the day.
